speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned sudden-onset vertigo; to help me determine the cause, have you noticed any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or double vision accompanying the spinning sensation?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since your symptoms resolved completely after just three minutes and you feel back to baseline, have you experienced any recent head trauma, severe headache, or limb weakness? Also, does the spinning sensation get triggered specifically when you turn your head or change your position?

REQUEST TEST: Vestibular_Swallow_Test

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical presentation of sudden, short-lived vertigo triggered by head movement, resolving to baseline, is classic for BPPV. The normal swallow test and lack of other neurological deficits support this.
